comments.body:
## Inventory

85 tracked files carry the token (ticket store excluded), confirmed exhaustive by an independent
blind sweep that returned ZERO hits for camelCase, space-separated, all seven non-ASCII hyphen
variants, and line-wrapped / implicitly-concatenated splits. Roughly 20 files need edits; the rest
are historical or pass-through-compatible.

- HISTORICAL, no change: ADRs 0043/0046/0049/0052/0059/0061/0098 and the generated ADR index;
  `CHANGELOG.md`; all of `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/` (harness, `runs/*.jsonl`,
  `runs/*.json` — frozen corpora whose filenames and `operator-attested-retag` labels are
  load-bearing); `docs/research/`; the captured-sample fixtures in
  `tests/fixtures/{cloud_adf,dc_wiki}_corpus/` (`scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py:47-52`
  states rewriting them falsifies the fixture).
- COMPATIBILITY, accept both: the canonical regex; `.rebar/criteria_routing.json:75` trigger;
  `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md`; recognition-side prompts
  (`completion_verifier.md`, `plan_review_evidence_kind.md`, `plan_review_ac_process_gate.md`);
  the eval-spec fixtures; `audit/page.py`; ~20 detector/close-guard tests that feed the old tag
  as input and assert on behavior.
- CUTOVER: `writing-a-passing-plan.md`; emit-side prompts E2/E6/F1; `coach_moves.py` move 14;
  `txn.py` + `completion_reconcile.py` message strings; the generated criteria guide (via its
  generator); the ~10 tests pinning those literal strings.

`operator-attested-retag` is a DIFFERENT token family (an edit-classification label in the
experiment harnesses) and must NOT be renamed.

## Implementation traps (each costs a review cycle if missed)

1. The widened alternation MUST be non-capturing: `\[(?:non-codebase|operator-attested)\]`. A
   capturing group turns `decide_ops.operator_attested_ac_texts`'s `findall()` into a list of
   TUPLES and breaks enrichment. Verified empirically.
2. `tests/unit/test_measurement_provenance_criterion.py` pins SHA256 digests AND exact line counts
   for contract text in five files. Its `_contract_lines()` selector keeps lines containing
   `"OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE"` or `"[operator-attested]"` — cut the prompts over without widening
   the selector and it matches ZERO lines, failing on the count assertion with a misleading
   "expected 1 contract line(s), found 0".
3. `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED
   (`python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide`) from the reviewer prompt
   `.md` files, and is gated three ways: `registry.validate_criteria_guide(...) == []` asserted in
   five test files, content pins in `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py`, and the digest
   pin above. Prompt edit + regeneration + pin updates must land in ONE commit.
4. `.rebar/criteria_routing.json:75` is an activation TRIGGER
   (`text_all: ["\\[operator-attested\\]"]`). Not widened => `[non-codebase]` plans SILENTLY skip
   `project.measurement-provenance` rather than erroring.
5. `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md:204` quotes the `coach_moves.py` move-14 template
   VERBATIM. Both must change identically or the guide misquotes real coach output.
6. The `[operator_attested]` underscore form is a DELIBERATE non-match asserted in ~15 places
   (ADR-0043 §46). `[non-codebase]` needs its own near-miss policy decided and tested.
7. Four further CI gates fire on files this touches and contain none of the token:
   `validate-routing`, the `reviewers/index.json` drift gate, `_eval-discipline.yml`, and
   `prompt-eval.yml`. `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` is a digest manifest with zero
   textual hits (it does not currently pin `evidence-kind` or `project.measurement-provenance`,
   so those two criteria alone will not break it).

compiled_state.description:
## Why

`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043) is the acceptance-criteria qualifier that tells the completion
verifier "this criterion's done-evidence inherently lives OUTSIDE the codebase, so accept a
recorded attestation instead of hunting for code proof".

The word `operator` mis-signals. Across this repo it means a *human specifically* — "the
operator runbook", "the operator guide", "the operator escape hatch", "the operator can" — and
the detector even carries a marker family named `human`. Agents therefore read
`[operator-attested]` as "a person must do this", when in fact an agent recording a Gerrit vote
outcome or a live-run result attests exactly as well. The tag names the wrong axis: WHO attests,
rather than WHERE the evidence lives.

Rename the canonical tag to `[non-codebase]`, the missing half of a pair the vocabulary already
has. `[codebase]` is ALREADY a recognized tag (ADR-0043 §exact-match; `completion_verifier.md:95`;
`plan_review_evidence_kind.md:56`; used on seven ACs of ticket 7226 in the corpus). It is
prompt-level only — no regex parses it — but it is established author vocabulary, so
`[non-codebase]` is not a coinage.

The new name also RESISTS the attestation-laundering anti-pattern by construction. To tag a
criterion whose proof is `tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py` (the live bug 2f56 case), an author
must assert that file is "non-codebase" — self-evidently false. The name does the
`det_attestation_launder` guard's work in the author's head before the guard ever runs.

`[operator-attested]` is RETAINED as an accepted but UNDOCUMENTED compatibility alias. This is
not optional: 827 of 4,285 tickets in the live store (19%) carry the tag. Those are immutable
event-sourced records; a hard cutover would silently reclassify every one of their attested ACs
as codebase-verifiable and break their close path.

## Scope decisions (operator-approved)

- The completion-verdict `kind` wire value `"operator-attested"` -> `"non-codebase"` IS in scope.
  Blast radius is ONE comparison site (`src/rebar/audit/page.py:329`); the schema declares `kind`
  as unconstrained `"type": "string"` with no enum. Sequenced reader-widen BEFORE emitter-change
  so legacy persisted verdicts keep rendering.
- Python identifiers are NOT renamed: the `det_operator_attested` module,
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE`, `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_AC_RE`, the `operator_attested` finding
  attribute, the `operator_attested_gaps` coverage key. This keeps the object-identity re-export
  seam and its tests untouched, and removes 5 files from the change set entirely
  (`det_citation.py`, `det_clarity.py`, `test_det_citation.py`, `test_decide_ops_seam.py`,
  `test_plan_review_portability.py` reference only the symbols, never the tag string).

## What makes this tractable

TWO deterministic matchers must be widened, not one: the shared Python regex, AND the separate
`.rebar/criteria_routing.json` `text_all` activation trigger that decides whether
`project.measurement-provenance` fires at all (a trigger not widened does not error — it
SILENTLY skips the criterion).

The `kind` wire-value rename has a READER site and EMITTER sites, and they are sequenced apart:
`src/rebar/audit/page.py:329` is the only READER (the sole comparison in the codebase); the
EMITTERS are `src/rebar/llm/contracts.py:116`, `src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json`,
and `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md`. Reader-widen lands first (S2) so the 827
live tickets holding legacy verdicts keep rendering when the emitter changes (S7).

FIVE consumers share the IDENTICAL compiled regex object, so widening that ONE pattern propagates
everywhere with no other code change. Four read it normally — verified: `decide_ops`,
`workflow_ops`, `det_attestation_launder`, and `det_measurement_provenance` each satisfy `is`
against `det_operator_attested._OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE`. The FIFTH,
`src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:547` (`ensure_ac_boxes_checked`), uses it with INVERTED semantics — a
match EXEMPTS an unchecked AC from the close block — so widening also makes an unchecked
`[non-codebase]` AC close-exempt. That is intended (the exemption is the tag's purpose) and is
pinned by an AC in S1 rather than left implicit.

The change needs no new branch anywhere — which is why
`det_floor.py` (793 of its 800-line hard cap) and `decide_ops.plan_review_decide` (complexity 21,
grandfathered at threshold 15) require no edits and neither gate fires.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The canonical tag matcher accepts `[non-codebase]` and `[operator-attested]`
      case-insensitively, rejects the `[operator_attested]` near-miss, and uses a NON-capturing
      alternation so `findall()` arity is unchanged — proved by a unit test asserting
      `operator_attested_ac_texts` returns a list of `str`, not tuples.
- [x] Every existing test that feeds `[operator-attested]` passes UNCHANGED, demonstrating the
      alias still works.
- [x] `[non-codebase]` and `[operator-attested]` produce identical outcomes across the plan-time
      lint, the laundering guard, the provenance guard, the AC-checkbox precheck, and the close
      path — proved by parametrizing those suites over both spellings.
- [x] `project.measurement-provenance` fires on a `[non-codebase]`-tagged plan (the
      `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` trigger was widened), proved by a test asserting the trigger
      matches both spellings.
- [x] Author-facing guidance emits `[non-codebase]` only; `[operator-attested]` appears in NO
      documented surface, enforced by a NEGATIVE test over the packaged guide.
- [x] `src/rebar/audit/page.py` renders a legacy `kind: "operator-attested"` verdict identically
      to a new `kind: "non-codebase"` one, proved by a test over both fixture shapes.
- [x] The recognition-side prompts (`completion_verifier.md`, `plan_review_evidence_kind.md`,
      `plan_review_ac_process_gate.md`, `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md`)
      instruct that BOTH spellings are recognized, so the LLM classification agrees with the
      deterministic matcher.
- [x] The EMITTED classification vocabulary is cut over in lockstep with the tag, so the
      deterministic matcher and the LLM's emitted `kind` cannot diverge: the verifier emits
      `kind: "non-codebase"` (`completion_verifier.md:224`), `contracts.py:116` and
      `completion_verdict.schema.json` declare it, and BOTH tag-bearing checklist rules in the
      packaged registry `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` are widened —
      `acceptance_items_classified` (:1241, the classification vocabulary) AND
      `evidence_kind_matches_tag` (:1245, which hard-codes "the exact case-insensitive
      [operator-attested] tag" and FIRES on an untagged external outcome; left un-widened it
      would flag a correctly `[non-codebase]`-tagged criterion as untagged, punishing authors
      for using the new tag).
      NOTE — two DIFFERENT files share the basename `criteria_routing.json` and must not be
      confused: the project overlay `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carries the `text_all`
      ACTIVATION TRIGGER (AC4), while the packaged registry
      `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` carries the CLASSIFICATION VOCABULARY
      (this AC). Each is edited for its own concern only.
- [x] A new ADR (0101) amends ADR-0043 to record the rename, why `operator` mis-signalled, why
      `attested` alone was rejected, and that `[operator-attested]` is retained as a deliberately
      UNDOCUMENTED alias. ADR-0043 itself is unmodified; the generated ADR index is regenerated.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, and the generated criteria guide is regenerated with
      its parity check and contract digests updated in the same commit.
compiled_state.title: Rename the [operator-attested] AC qualifier to [non-codebase]
